inspiration: repipe round 9 need pe-zero-filled-data; the same omission the PE header page had one paragraph earlier -- a mapping unit the OS creates and object's neutral view does not describe
decisions: The filed hypothesis is UPHELD and exact: 'the read path may use file-backed length instead of PE virtual size'. ObjectLoadImage copies seg.data() (for a PE, min(VirtualSize, SizeOfRawData) bytes) into each Segment and find_section measures the segment as data.len(), so .data at RVA 0x8000 was mapped 0x200 bytes wide instead of 0x7a8. 0x140008740 fell past it, loadFill took its offset==0 break, and kuna-cli/src/disassemble.rs rendered the resulting DataUnavail as 'no loaded segment covers it'.

It is not a PE-specific fix, and was not written as one. seg.size() is the RAM footprint in all three backends object presents (ELF p_memsz, PE VirtualSize, Mach-O vmsize), so recording it on the Segment fixes ELF .bss with the same three lines: `kuna read fauxware 0x601058` goes from the same error to eight zero bytes, and 0x601060 -- exactly p_memsz -- still refuses.

The metadata already told the truth. segment_info (getSegments) and sections have carried seg.size() since they were written, so kuna's section walk, executable ranges and get_readonly ranges already covered the tail; only the byte-reading path disagreed with them. That is why the change closes the gap without moving a section flag or a discovery range.

The tail is recorded only for a segment the image marks as DATA, and that carve-out is measured, not defensive. Mapping an executable uninitialized region turns UPX0 (VirtualSize 0x9000 over SizeOfRawData 0) into 36 KB of readable zeroes inside an executable range: on the in-repo upx_packed_pe_i386.exe the packed entry stopped reporting `Unable to load 512 bytes at r0x00401d91` and decompiled to 16,883 lines of `add [eax],al` in 19.6 s, against 182 ms and a one-line honest refusal before. That is a worse answer than the one it replaced -- the move that helps there is `kuna unpack` -- so segment_bits CODE segments keep memsz 0 and behave exactly as they do today.

A segment whose file backs nothing at all is now kept rather than dropped as empty (`data.is_empty() && seg.size() == 0`). Without it a SizeOfRawData 0 section -- UPX0, an ELF .bss in its own PT_LOAD -- would still map nothing, which is the same defect at the limit.

The footprint is trimmed at the next segment's vma, but only the tail: `memsz.min(room).max(data.len())`. The min alone would map 0 bytes for every segment of a COFF .obj read through the linked path, which stacks all of them at vma 0; the max keeps every file extent exactly as wide as it was.

No phases.toml option. A mapping unit the OS creates is not a judgement call, the CLAUDE.md rule scopes options to what can change emitted C, and the change is measured byte-identical on every image that loads today. Same disposition as the sibling loader fix #458, which added the PE header page.

The cost of the carve-out is that an image whose only load segment is RWX does not get its .bss read either. Conservative in the right direction, and the address still resolves through the section walk, which has always described the whole footprint.

sweep.method: A/B by binary: the patched release kuna against the one built from the recorded base commit 8df2a52e, same specs, same options
sweep.decompile_all_detail: the reported KeyCheker.exe, 4 other round-8 arena targets (a 1587-function ELF, a UPX-packed ELF, 2 PEs) and 4 in-repo fixtures (ELF exec, CET PIE, PE with imports, COFF .obj)
sweep.unpack_detail: upx_packed_pe_i386.exe, upx_packed_x86_64, upx_packed_lzma_x86_64 -- output images byte-identical. The UPX PE is the sharpest case for this change: its .text is VirtualSize 0x9000 over SizeOfRawData 0, executable, so it goes from mapping nothing to mapping 36 KB of zeroes inside an executable range. `functions --json` on it is byte-identical, i.e. the recursive-descent walk does not start decoding the zeroes.
sweep.why_not: the section flags, the executable ranges and the read-only ranges are all derived from metadata that already carried the RAM footprint, so nothing that classifies an address moved; the only new answers are byte reads at addresses that previously had none, and a read of writable zero-initialized memory is not folded
sweep.upx_detail: upx_packed_pe_i386.exe, upx_packed_x86_64, upx_packed_lzma_x86_64: `kuna unpack` output images and `decompile-all` byte-identical, 182 ms vs 175 ms on the PE. This is the case the DATA carve-out exists for; without it the same command took 19.6 s and emitted 16,883 lines.
sweep.decompile_all_fixtures_detail: the first 80 of the 144 loadable in-repo fixtures, byte-identical; the run was cut short of the remaining 64 for time, and the 144-fixture `functions --json` and 9-binary `decompile-all` passes below are complete
sweep.subset_argument: the DATA carve-out maps a strict subset of what the un-carved version mapped, and the un-carved version was measured byte-identical on the 9-binary `decompile-all` and 144-fixture `functions --json` passes, so on those images the carved version answers the same as the base at every address
